title: The new SAFE food safety grading framework and how it will work
asked: Four MPs asked about the Safety Assurance for Food Establishments (SAFE) framework: how it addresses public health risks and how its effectiveness will be measured, how grading stays transparent and accessible once physical decals are replaced by digital disclosures, whether reduced inspections are driven by manpower limits, and what support small businesses get.
asked_by: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms Poh Li San
response: Mr Zaqy Mohamad said SAFE grades food establishments A, B or C based on their food safety track record from SFA inspections, with the first phase starting 19 January 2026. Category 1 outlets that want Grade A must implement a Food Safety Management System and appoint an Advanced Food Hygiene Officer, while those convicted of a major lapse or suspended after 12 demerit points are downgraded to Grade C. Inspections continue under a targeted, data-driven regime, with larger-scale and Grade C outlets inspected more frequently, and consumers can scan the QR code on a licence for real-time grade information. Support includes SkillsFuture subsidies of up to 70% for AFHO training and up to 50% Enterprise Development Grant support for SMEs certifying their FSMS.

key_points.point: SAFE is rolled out in two phases, with the first starting 19 January 2026
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: It will be implemented in two phases, with the first phase implemented on 19 January 2026.

key_points.point: Category 1 covers larger-scale operations such as food manufacturers, caterers, central kitchens and large restaurants; hawker stalls, small restaurants and bakeries are Category 2
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: Category 1 food establishments are those with a larger scale of food processing or preparation

key_points.point: Establishments need no extra requirements unless they are Category 1 and want Grade A
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: They do not have to fulfil any additional requirements, unless they are Category 1 food establishments that wish to attain Grade A.

key_points.point: A major lapse with a court conviction, or suspension after 12 demerit points, means a drop to Grade C
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: will be downgraded to Grade C, regardless of their existing grade

key_points.point: Larger-scale and Grade C establishments are inspected more often
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: Food establishments with a larger scale of food processing or preparation, as well as those with Grade C, will be inspected more frequently.

key_points.point: Scanning the QR code on a licence gives real-time grade and track record information instead of annually updated decals
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: This mitigates the risk of outdated decals being displayed at the premises.

key_points.point: AFHO training applicants get SkillsFuture Singapore subsidies of up to 70%
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: Individuals who apply for the AFHO training course will receive SkillsFuture Singapore subsidies of up to 70%.

key_points.point: SFA partnered with IMDA on Seniors Go Digital to teach seniors to scan SAFE QR codes
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: SFA has also partnered with the Infocomm Media Development Authority on the Seniors Go Digital programme to teach seniors on how to use their phone cameras to scan the SAFE QR codes at food establishments.

key_points.point: There are about 45,000 licensees under the regime, so tracing is done on a risk basis
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: we have about 45,000 licensees under this regime, both Category 1 and Category 2

key_points.point: No self-declaration is required for Category 1 and Category 2 classification; data comes from licensing and SFA inspections
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: for Category 1 and Category 2 classification as an example, there is no self declaration required

key_points.point: Government procurement requires a minimum of Grade B in some contracts
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: Government procurement is one good example in which there is a minimum of Grade B in the criteria to be procured under Government contracts.

key_points.point: SFA's Point Demerit System triggers suspension
key_points.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
key_points.quote: For SFA, we have a Point Demerit System.

left_open: A specific revised inspection frequency figure
The transition duration and the resources SFA needs to complete inspections under the new grading system
Whether the shift away from regular inspections is driven by manpower constraints
Specific outcome-based indicators such as outbreak severity or recurrence rates
Whether a physical decal requirement will be reinstated as grades change
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered digital access to grades, outcome-based effectiveness measures, upstream food-chain risks, audit verification and persistently poor-performing outlets
